title: Subtype-Specific In-Hospital Outcomes and Robotic Adoption in Thoracic Outlet Decompression: A US National Inpatient Sample Study, 2016–2023
content: Background and Objectives: National comparisons of thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) decompression outcomes by subtype rely mainly on data from before 2016, and national use of robotic assistance has not been described. We compared in-hospital morbidity and resource use by subtype and described robotic assistance. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included adult hospitalizations with a TOS-related diagnosis and a decompression procedure in the 2016–2023 National Inpatient Sample. Algorithm-defined venous and arterial TOS were compared with neurogenic TOS using survey-weighted logistic, quasi-Poisson, and gamma regression adjusted for prespecified covariates. The primary outcome was a coded postprocedural complication composite; secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), nonroutine discharge, and total charges. Results: The 2,594 hospitalizations represented an estimated 12,970 nationally (59.3% female; neurogenic, 60.5%; venous, 33.7%; arterial, 5.8%). The primary composite occurred in 5.0%, 8.4%, and 13.2%, respectively (joint p < 0.001), with adjusted odds ratios of 1.69 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.20–2.36) for venous and 3.21 (95% CI, 1.82–5.68) for arterial TOS. Additional adjustment for admission type and same-stay vascular treatment attenuated the venous association (1.42; 95% CI, 0.94–2.14), whereas the arterial association persisted (2.81; 95% CI, 1.56–5.07). Both vascular subtypes had longer LOS (rate ratios, 2.37 and 2.24), more nonroutine discharge, and higher mean charges (ratios, 2.17 and 2.45). Coded robotic assistance increased from 3.5% in 2016–2017 to 8.6% in 2023 (adjusted odds ratio per year, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06–1.30). In exploratory post hoc analyses, adjusted mean charges were higher with robotic assistance (ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.25–1.71), whereas morbidity and LOS comparisons were inconclusive. Conclusions: Algorithm-defined vascular TOS was associated with greater coded in-hospital morbidity and resource use than neurogenic TOS; the venous complication excess was attenuated by adjustment for care-pathway factors, whereas the arterial excess persisted. Robotic assistance is increasing, but its comparative outcomes remain uncertain.
